ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a uniform magnetic field directed into the plane of the paper, with a magnetic induction strength of $B = 0.8\mathrm{T}$. The magnetic field has a distinct circular boundary with the center at point O and a radius of 1 cm. Circular coils are placed sequentially on the plane of the paper, all centered at point O: coil A has a radius of 1 cm and 1 turn; coil B has a radius of 2 cm and 1 turn; coil C has a radius of 0.5 cm and 1 turn.

1. In the process where the magnetic induction intensity $B$ decreases to 0.4T, how much does the magnetic flux in A and B change respectively?
2. By how much does the magnetic flux in C change as the direction of the magnetic field rotates through an angle of $30^{\circ}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows three concentric circular coils centered at O. The largest outer circle is labeled B. A smaller circular coil whose radius matches the cross-marked magnetic-field boundary is labeled A. Inside it there is a still smaller concentric circle labeled C. The crosses indicate a magnetic field directed into the paper, confined to the circular region of radius 1 cm. Reasoning: The magnetic field exists only inside the circular boundary of radius 1 cm. Coil A has radius 1 cm, so it links exactly that field area. Coil B has radius 2 cm, but the field outside radius 1 cm is zero, so B also links only the same field area. Thus for A and B, the effective area is S = π(0.01 m)^2. When B decreases from 0.8 T to 0.4 T, the magnitude of the change is ΔB = 0.4 T, so |ΔΦ_A| = |ΔΦ_B| = ΔB·S = 0.4π(0.01)^2 = 1.256×10^-4 Wb. For coil C, its radius is 0.5 cm = 0.005 m, and it lies fully inside the magnetic-field region, so S_C = π(0.005)^2. Initially the field is perpendicular to the coil plane, so Φ_initial = B S_C. After the field direction rotates by 30°, the flux is Φ_final = B S_C cos30°. Therefore |ΔΦ_C| = B S_C(1 - cos30°) = 0.8π(0.005)^2(1 - cos30°) ≈ 8.4×10^-6 Wb.
